footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $9,617M; this page starts from gross revenue of $13,246M so the $3,629M of client incentives shows as a cost.
oneTimers: The GAAP litigation provision was just $10M this quarter (versus $129M a year ago); Visa excludes litigation provisions from its non-GAAP results, which is most of why non-GAAP net income of $5,425M sits above the GAAP $5,318M.
otherDetail: Investment income and other income of $199M, partly offset by $176M of interest expense on Visa's debt.

takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 12% to $9,617M as the growth drivers held steady: payments volume +8%, cross-border volume +13% and processed transactions +10% in constant dollars. Every revenue line grew, with Other revenue up 30%.
takeaways.title: A strong finish to the fiscal year

takeaways.text: Net income rose 14% to $5,318M and EPS 17% to $2.65 — helped by a small $10M litigation provision versus $129M a year ago, and by buybacks shrinking the share count. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.71.
takeaways.title: Profit grew faster than revenue

takeaways.text: Visa returned $6.8B to shareholders in the quarter through buybacks and dividends, and raised the quarterly dividend 13% to $0.59 a share.
takeaways.title: Cash kept flowing back

verdict: Visa closed its fiscal year with net revenue up 12% to $9.6B on steady card spending — payments volume rose 8% and cross-border volume 13% — and net income grew 14% to $5.3B.
